international.notes: The university has a Dirección de Relaciones Internacionales. Its 2026 inbound-exchange factsheet requires Spanish B2 and says Health Faculty students may take theoretical subjects; clinical placements require special mobility agreements. I found no official evidence that Medicina is taught in English.

profile_paragraphs: The Facultad de Ciencias de la Salud was created by Rectoral Resolution No. 100/2008. It groups health programmes across Santiago, Talca and Temuco; Medicine is one of its undergraduate programmes.

Medicine is a seven-year, daytime, in-person programme taught at Campus Providencia (Santiago), Talca and Temuco. The official graduate profile describes a general physician-surgeon with a community and family-health orientation.

The faculty’s currently listed medical specialties are Imaging, Family Medicine, Emergency Medicine and Internal Medicine. No rheumatology specialty appears on that official list; no university rheumatology unit was located.

Clinical teaching links include the hospitals of Linares and Parral, Hospital Parroquial San Bernardo and Hospital Clínico FACH. This provides teaching-hospital exposure, but the university’s current public vacancy page showed no academic opening on the research date.

For international engagement, the university operates a dedicated International Relations office and has a specific Medicine/Enfermería mobility agreement with the Universidad del País Vasco. Incoming health exchanges are normally limited to theoretical courses and require Spanish B2.
